title: Module and local Hom transport under a ringed-topos equivalence
statement: Let $e:(\mathscr X,R)\to(\mathscr X',R')$ be an equivalence of ringed topoi presented by small sites, where $R,R'$ are sheaves of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]: its underlying geometric morphism is an equivalence and $e^{-1}R'\to R$ is an isomorphism. The module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] is an exact equivalence $e^*\dashv e_*$ of module-sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Termwise application gives mutually inverse equivalences of unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], preserving K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. For every sheaf of sets $V'$ in $\mathscr X'$, the induced equivalence on the slice topoi [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction] over $V'$ and $e^{-1}V'$ has these same properties for the restricted rings. Slice over a site object means slice over its sheafified representable [lem-weil-pbc-localized-sheaves-over-representable]. These equivalences commute with further restrictions, derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and localization of the restricted ring at a section [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. For every $N\in D(R')$ and every ideal subsheaf $\mathcal I'\subset R'$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-ideal-generators], put $\mathcal I=e^*\mathcal I'$. Then the tests $R\mathcal Hom(R'|_{V'}[1/a],N|_{V'})=0$ for all site objects $V'$ and $a\in\mathcal I'(V')$ hold if and only if the tests $R\mathcal Hom(R|_V[1/b],e^*N|_V)=0$ hold for all site objects $V$ of the other presentation and $b\in\mathcal I(V)$.

proof.text: Put $F=e^*$ and $G=e_*$. Because the structural ring map is invertible, $FM$ is $e^{-1}M$ with its transported $R$-action, by the tensor formula in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Transport the addition, zero, inverse and scalar-action maps through the inverse equivalence of sheaves of sets; preservation of products ensures that all their defining diagrams remain commutative. This gives an inverse on module objects. Its unit and counit are the underlying equivalence isomorphisms and are linear, since the action maps were transported along them. The module adjunction therefore has invertible unit and counit. Both functors preserve sums of morphisms (addition is the diagonal followed by the product of the two maps followed by module addition). An additive equivalence preserves kernels and cokernels by their universal properties, hence is exact in the abelian categories of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules, Tag 03D7; explicit equivalence argument for an invertible structural map

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to the exact functors $F,G$. Their termwise unit and counit give inverse isomorphisms of complexes, and hence inverse natural isomorphisms after localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This produces mutually inverse equivalences on the unbounded derived categories, represented termwise. Exactness gives $H^n(FK)\cong F H^n(K)$ and the analogous equality for $G$, so acyclicity and zero objects are preserved and reflected; no boundedness is used.

source.place: derived-category localization and exact termwise functors; natural unit and counit specialized to an equivalence

proof.text: If $I$ is K-injective and $C$ is acyclic, the termwise equivalence identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(R)}(C,FI)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(R')}(GC,I)=0$, since $GC$ is acyclic. The identification respects homotopies: applying an additive functor to $f=dh+hd$ gives $Ff=(Fd)(Fh)+(Fh)(Fd)$. This is exactly K-injectivity [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Interchanging $F,G$ proves the converse and preservation in the other direction.

For a sheaf $A'$ put $A=e^{-1}A'$. On slices the functor sends $(T'\to A')$ to $(e^{-1}T'\to A)$; its inverse applies $e_*$ and then the equivalence unit to identify $e_*A$ with $A'$. The original unit and counit give inverse natural isomorphisms on these slices. The restricted ring is $R_A=R\times A\to A$, which is identified with the inverse image of $R'_{A'}$ because $e^{-1}$ preserves products. Use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction] for the small element-site presentations and their rings. Steps 1-3 apply to these ringed equivalences. For $B'\to A'$, both iterated restrictions send a sheaf to its product with $e^{-1}B'$ over $e^{-1}A'$; the product comparison gives their canonical isomorphism. For a site object $U$, [lem-weil-pbc-localized-sheaves-over-representable] identifies this construction over $h_U^\#$ with the localized site $\mathcal C/U$, without assuming subcanonicity.

proof.text:
Here is the derived internal Hom comparison, on the whole topos and on each slice of step 4. Exactness means that $F$ computes $Le^*$: applying $F$ to a K-flat resolution gives a quasi-isomorphism to the termwise image. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], $F$ preserves derived tensor. For every $C\in D(R)$ the equivalence of step 2 and the closed adjunction of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] give natural bijections
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}(C,F R\mathcal Hom(L,M))&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(GC,R\mathcal Hom(L,M))\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(GC\otimes^{\mathbf L}L,M)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C\otimes^{\mathbf L}FL,FM)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C,R\mathcal Hom(FL,FM)).
\end{aligned}$$
The third bijection uses $FGC\cong C$ and tensor preservation. Applying the natural bijection and its inverse to the respective identity morphisms produces mutually inverse arrows, so $F R\mathcal Hom(L,M)\cong R\mathcal Hom(FL,FM)$, naturally in $L,M$.

proof.text:
To justify restriction of this calculation and the local tests to arbitrary sheaves, use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]. Since $j_{A!}$ is exact and left adjoint to restriction, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] shows that $j_A^*I$ is K-injective whenever $I$ is. On the element site, further slicing at $(U,s)$ gives $\mathcal C/U$: an object over $(U,s)$ is uniquely an arrow $V\to U$, its section being forced to be the restriction of $s$. Thus the sheaf Hom formula of [def-pur-sheaf-hom] gives
$$j_A^*\mathcal Hom_R(L^p,I^q)\cong\mathcal Hom_{R_A}(j_A^*L^p,j_A^*I^q).$$
Restriction commutes with products (both sides evaluate at $(U,s)$ as the product of the values at $U$). It therefore commutes with the Hom complex of [def-pur-hom-complex], including its differential $d\phi=d_I\phi-(-1)^n\phi d_L$. Compute derived Hom with $I$ by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; its restricted complex is a valid K-injective representative, giving $j_A^*R\mathcal Hom_R(L,M)\cong R\mathcal Hom_{R_A}(j_A^*L,j_A^*M)$. Applying this inside a slice proves the same assertion for every further restriction. These comparisons agree for two successive restrictions because on every $(V,t)$ they are the same restriction of linear maps and the same differential.

proof.text: The localization in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization] is the colimit of the multiplication sequence $R\xrightarrow a R\xrightarrow a\cdots$ in module sheaves, as spelled out in [def-weil-pbc-local-coefficient-localization]. The global-section version on any element site has the same description: send $r$ at stage $n$ to $r/a^n$ in sectionwise localization; the fraction relations are exactly the filtered-colimit relations, and module sheafification is left adjoint to inclusion, hence computes the sheaf colimit. Both $F$ on a slice and restriction $j_B^*$ preserve these colimits: the first is an equivalence, and the second is the module pullback left adjoint to module pushforward by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Their ring comparisons send multiplication by $a$ to multiplication by its image. Consequently they identify the localization and its map from the ring, $F(R'_{A'}[1/a])\cong R_A[1/Fa]$, and likewise after every further restriction. The comparison is fixed by the maps of the multiplication sequence, so agrees for iterated restrictions.

proof.text: First express the tests independently of a chosen generating family. Suppose they hold on every object $U$ of a given site. For any sheaf $A$ and section $a:A\to\mathcal I$, form $Z=R\mathcal Hom_{R_A}(R_A[1/a],N|_A)$. On the element site of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction], restriction at $(U,s)$ identifies $Z|_{(U,s)}$, by steps 6-7, with $R\mathcal Hom_{R_U}(R_U[1/a(s)],N|_U)=0$, since $a(s)\in\mathcal I(U)$. For each $n$, restriction is exact, so $(H^nZ)|_{(U,s)}=0$. Evaluating at the terminal object of that localized site shows $(H^nZ)(U,s)=0$. Every value of every cohomology sheaf is therefore zero, and $Z=0$ in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Conversely, the arbitrary-sheaf tests include the original tests by taking $A=h_U^\#$, using [lem-weil-pbc-localized-sheaves-over-representable]. Thus the two testing conventions are equivalent. This argument also covers an empty element site or an empty covering.

source.place: Definition 0999, definition-derived-complete, and opening reduction of Tag 099J, lemma-pushforward-derived-complete; explicit arbitrary-sheaf testing argument

proof.text: For $A=e^{-1}A'$, full faithfulness identifies sections $a:A'\to\mathcal I'$ with sections $b:A\to e^{-1}\mathcal I'=\mathcal I$; the equality uses the invertible structural ring map, so these are the same ideal elements under the transported action [def-weil-pbc-ringed-ideal-generators]. Steps 5 and 7 identify the two corresponding derived Hom objects. They vanish simultaneously because the equivalence on the slice preserves and reflects zero objects. Every sheaf $A$ is isomorphic to the inverse image of some $A'$, and this identification also transports every section of $\mathcal I$. Hence all arbitrary-sheaf tests hold on one side exactly when they hold on the other. Apply step 8 in each presentation to obtain precisely the two families of site-object tests in the statement. This proves the last clause for every $N\in D(R')$ and every ideal sheaf, without finite-generation or boundedness assumptions.
